title: Dianthus genomic DNA extraction
author: Jesús icazo-Aragonés
materials: In the meantime, prepare 2 mL Eppendorf tubes with 2-3 glass beads (4 mm) and 100 mg of tissue and transfer tubes into liquid nitrogen. This is the easiest with fresh tissue because freeze thawing is avoided during cutting. However, if there is no other way, tissue frozen in liquid nitrogen (ensuring it stays frozen) also works. 100 mg, Tissue (COOL DOWN CENTRIFUGE TO 4ºC AND HEAT UP THE THERMOBLOCK TO 37ºC FOR NEXT STEPS)

Before grinding make sure tissue is completely frozen in liquid nitrogen and perform the grinding steps as quickly as possible to avoid freeze thawing. The grinding rack can also be frozen to ensure that (it is highly recommended to store it at -80°C for at least 3 hours, overnight if possible). Grind the tissue using an automated grinder (Qiagen TissueLyzer II) for 30 seconds (actual grinding time may differ from tissue to tissue). Immediately put the tube into liquid nitrogen. If the tissue is not well ground, repeat this step until it is (grinding is crucial for the extraction). 00:00:30, Grinding Alternatively, grind the frozen material manually with a mortar.

Transfer the DNA solutions into one tube and add TE buffer to make up a total volume of 500 µL. If the extraction is done with multiple tubes at a time (which is usually the case), then after the elution step all the eluted DNA can just be pipetted into one tube.

steps.title: Prepare fresh lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Make 10 mL of lysis buffer fresh, adding all components as listed, and heat to 64 °C for 30 min; after cooling to room temperature add RNase A (1 µL per 1 mL lysis buffer, i.e., 10 µL or 5 µL).

substeps.instruction: 1 % PVP‑40: 0.1 g in 1 mL stock, add 500 µL stock (final 0.05 %).
1 % PVP‑10: 0.1 g in 1 mL stock, add 500 µL stock (final 0.05 %).
500 mM NaCl: 0.2922 g in 1 mL 5 M stock, add 500 µL stock (final 250 mM).
100 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8: 1 M stock, add 500 µL (final 50 mM).
50 mM EDTA: 0.5 M stock, add 500 µL (final 25 mM).
1.25 % SDS (2 g SDS in 100 mL): 20 % stock, add 312.5 µL (final 0.625 %).
5 mM DTT: 0.077 g in 500 µL 1 M stock, add 12.5 µL (final 0.5 mM).
Milli‑Q water: add 2.16 mL to bring volume to 4.3 mL.
Heat the complete buffer at 64 °C for 30 min, then cool to room temperature.
Add RNase A (1 µL per 1 mL lysis buffer; use 10 µL or 5 µL as appropriate).

steps.title: Add preheated buffer to tissue
steps.instruction: Add 700 µL of the pre‑heated lysis buffer to each tube containing frozen Dianthus tissue and invert until no frozen clumps remain (may take several minutes).

steps.title: Incubate at 37 °C
steps.instruction: Place tubes in a thermomixer set to 37 °C, shaking at 400 rpm (slowly) for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Cool on ice
steps.instruction: Remove tubes from the thermomixer and cool on ice for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Add proteinase K
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL proteinase K to each tube and incubate at 37 °C in the thermomixer for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Add potassium acetate
steps.instruction: Add 210 µL (≈0.3 vol) of 5 M potassium acetate, invert the tube 20 times, then keep on ice (~4 °C) for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Centrifuge lysate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge tubes at 6000 g for 20 minutes at 4 °C.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully transfer the supernatant (~600 µL) to a new 1.5 mL tube without disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Add magnetic beads
steps.instruction: Add 1 volume (~600 µL) of bead solution (room‑temperature, vortexed for ~30 seconds beforehand) to the transferred supernatant.

steps.title: Bind DNA to beads
steps.instruction: Invert to mix, then incubate on a rotor for 10 minutes at room temperature (pre‑heat TE buffer to 50 °C in parallel).

steps.title: Quick spin
steps.instruction: Spin the tube for 1 second to collect liquid at the bottom.

steps.title: Magnetic separation
steps.instruction: Place the tube in a magnetic rack for 5 minutes until beads are immobilized and the solution becomes clear.

steps.title: Remove supernatant
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant without disturbing the beads.

steps.title: First ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL fresh 70 % ethanol, wait 30 seconds, then remove the supernatant without disturbing the beads.

steps.title: Second ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Repeat the addition of 1 mL 70 % ethanol, wait 30 seconds, and remove the supernatant as before.

steps.title: Final bead spin
steps.instruction: Spin the tube for 1 second and keep it on the magnetic rack to eliminate remaining ethanol.

steps.title: Air‑dry beads
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the beads for 30 seconds (do not exceed this time).

steps.title: Elute DNA from beads
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL TE buffer pre‑heated to 50 °C, flick the tube to resuspend beads until no aggregates remain.

steps.title: Incubate elution
steps.instruction: Incubate the resuspended beads at room temperature for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Collect eluate
steps.instruction: Spin 1 second, place on magnetic rack, incubate 5–10 minutes until solution is clear, then transfer the supernatant (eluted DNA) to a new tube.

steps.title: Chloroform extraction
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL (1 vol) chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (24:1), invert the tube about 100 times (≥2 minutes).

steps.title: Phase separation centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 8000 g, 4 °C for 10 minutes; if the aqueous phase remains cloudy, centrifuge again at 6000 g, 4 °C for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Collect aqueous phase
steps.instruction: Transfer the upper (aqueous) phase to a new tube and discard the lower chloroform phase (one round is usually sufficient).

steps.title: Add sodium acetate
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL (0.1 vol) 3 M sodium acetate, invert the tube 10–20 times.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL (2 vol) ice‑cold (‑20 °C) 100 % ethanol, invert gently a few times, then incubate at ‑20 °C overnight (or 1–2 hours for a faster protocol).

steps.title: Pellet DNA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 5000 g, 4 °C for 5 minutes (pre‑heat TE buffer to 50 °C while centrifuging).

steps.title: Recover supernatant
steps.instruction: Pipette the supernatant off the opposite side of the pellet, keep it, and centrifuge the recovered supernatant at 5000 g, 4 °C for 10 minutes; store supernatant at 4 °C or ‑20 °C for later use if needed.

steps.title: Ethanol wash pellet
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL ice‑cold 70 % ethanol to the pellet, mix gently.

steps.title: Wash centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 4500 g, 4 °C for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Remove ethanol
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Repeat ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Repeat the addition of 1 mL ice‑cold 70 % ethanol, centrifugation (4500 g, 4 °C, 15 min), and removal of supernatant to ensure all ethanol is removed.

steps.title: Final air‑dry
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the pellet for 2–5 minutes, or until no ethanol residue remains.

steps.title: Final DNA elution
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL TE buffer pre‑heated to 50 °C, resuspend the pellet; incubate until fully dissolved (overnight at room temperature if pellet is large).

steps.title: Quantify DNA
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration with Qubit and absorbance with NanoDrop; A260/280 should be 1.8–2.0, A260/230 should be 2.0–2.0 (Qubit optional if cleanup performed).

steps.title: Verify DNA quality
steps.instruction: Measure Qubit and NanoDrop again and run an agarose gel to confirm sample cleanliness and absence of fragmentation.
